title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Drones sink a ship off a NATO member's coast
preheader: Bulgaria halted the search for the missing crew, so the death toll is still unknown.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, October 07, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 1 update on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Drones hit two cargo ships off Bulgaria, sinking one
stories.why_important: Unidentified drones hit two cargo ships in Bulgaria's Black Sea economic zone. The drones hit them on Tuesday, sinking one and leaving its crew missing. Bulgaria is a NATO member, and this is the first drone attack on shipping in its waters. The government has not blamed Moscow, but the opposition says it should.
stories.what_overlooked: Bulgaria stopped searching for the missing crew on Wednesday, Vice-Admiral Rumen Nikolov told Nova TV. So the death toll from the sinking is still unknown.
stories.prediction: If Bulgaria or NATO names the drone's origin, that will decide if this stays a rescue story or becomes a NATO response.

stories.story_title: Germany arrests its former spy chief on treason charges
stories.why_important: German prosecutors detained August Hanning on suspicion of passing state secrets to a foreign intelligence service. He led the BND from 1998 to 2005. His former bureau chief was arrested with him. A former top spy facing treason charges is rare and damaging for Germany's security services.
stories.what_overlooked: German media say the foreign service was not Russian. Haaretz reports the evidence came from a Danish investigation into an heiress's abducted children that involved former Israeli agents.
stories.prediction: Prosecutors must soon decide whether to formally charge Hanning or release him. A charge sheet would name the foreign intelligence service.

stories.story_title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as Congo's outbreak spreads
stories.why_important: A Kenyan man who travelled from eastern Congo via Uganda died of Ebola in Nairobi, Kenya's first confirmed case. Congo's outbreak is the second largest on record, with more than 8,000 cases, and Uganda has already had 20. Kenya's health system now faces its own first outbreak.
stories.what_overlooked: The man crossed at least one international border before he died. Kenya is the fourth country linked to Congo's outbreak, which shows how easily the virus gets past border screening.
stories.prediction: Kenya's health ministry will report whether the dead man's contacts test positive. A cluster would mean local transmission, not an imported case.

quick_hits.text: A naval drone set a Liberian-flagged tanker ablaze off Sochi, and Russia said it rescued all 23 crew, all Indian nationals.
US Vice President JD Vance said Iran must make a 'meaningful' cut to its uranium enrichment capacity to end the seven-month war.
Israel marked three years since the October 7 attack with memorials, new strikes on Gaza and election campaigning weeks before a vote.
The UAE revoked two Israeli airlines' landing rights, ending repatriation flights, after a flydubai co-pilot allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound plane.
Kim Jong Un pledged continued support for Russia's war in a birthday message to Putin, while state media condemned US F-16 sales to Taiwan.
Trump said he has a call scheduled with Vladimir Putin to discuss Russia's suspected pneumonic plague case.

big_number.context: Paramount Skydance's completed takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, which Reuters says creates the largest Hollywood studio owner in years.
